title: The Language of Chemistry — Investigating Matter, Chapter 6
eyebrow: CKSci Grade 5 · Investigating Matter · Chapter 6 · Student Reader pp. 33–38
bigQuestion: What are atoms, elements, and molecules?

mission.name: Chapter 6 review
mission.blurb: A quick check that the chapter landed — not a test.

items.q: What does the book say chemistry is the science of?
opts: What matter is made of and how matter changes
How living things grow, feed and reproduce
The movement of the planets and the stars
How heat travels from one place to another
items.why: Chemistry is the science of what matter is made of and how matter changes. And no one person thought it up — the ideas were shared and built on, from the ancient Greeks to today.

items.q: Democritus and Leucippus built the word atom out of two Greek pieces. What did they mean by it?
opts: Not to cut — a particle that cannot be cut smaller
Not to see — a particle too small for any eye
To join — a particle that sticks to other particles
To burn — a particle released by fire
items.why: The Greek prefix a- means “not,” and temnein means “to cut.” Put them together and you get atomos — “not to cut.” Atoms became the new word for particles that could not be cut any smaller.

items.q: The ancient Greeks and John Dalton both said matter is made of atoms. What did Dalton do that they did not?
opts: He studied evidence from chemical reactions
He gave the particles the name we still use
He looked at matter through a microscope
He was the first to suggest atoms exist
items.why: The Greeks did not use a scientific process for examining ideas for supporting evidence — they did not determine whether their ideas were true or false. Dalton, unlike them, studied evidence from chemical reactions. It took about two thousand years before there was evidence to support the atomic theory.

items.q: What did Dalton add to Democritus’s idea?
opts: Some atoms are alike and some are different
Atoms can be cut into still smaller pieces
Atoms are far too small ever to be counted
All atoms in the universe are exactly alike
items.why: Dalton's atomic theory was built upon the ideas of Democritus: that atoms are tiny particles that cannot be further cut. But Dalton added to this idea. Dalton said that some atoms are alike and some are different, and that when atoms join, they make up different types of matter.

items.q: Match each word to the meaning the book gives it.
pairs: The science of what matter is made of and how matter changes
A small particle of chemical matter
A substance made of a single type of atom
A connection that holds atoms together
A substance made of one or more kinds of atoms joined together by chemical bonds
items.why: These five are the chapter's Core Vocabulary. Everything else in the chapter is built out of them: atoms are the pieces, an element is matter made of one kind of piece, a bond is what holds pieces together, and a molecule is what you get when they are held together.

items.q: All the glowing gas in a neon sign is one kind of atom. What does that make neon?
opts: An element
A molecule
A mixture
A precipitate
items.why: When all the atoms in matter are the same, the matter is called an element. All of the glowing gas in a neon sign is made of one kind of atom — neon. In the same way, every atom in a gold nugget is an atom of the element gold.

items.q: Two hydrogen atoms join with one oxygen atom. What have you got?
opts: A molecule of water
An element called water
A mixture of two gases
A precipitate
items.why: When one or more kinds of atoms form chemical bonds with other atoms, they form molecules. Two hydrogen atoms often join with one oxygen atom — and when this happens, you get a molecule of a substance you use every day. Water. It is not an element, because the atoms are not all the same kind.

items.q: Sort each one by whether it is an element or a molecule.
bins: An element — one type of atom
chips: The glowing gas in a neon sign
items.why: The test is whether the atoms are all the same kind. Neon and gold are elements — every atom in them is the same. Water, carbon dioxide and protein are molecules — different kinds of atoms bonded together.

items.q: Which of these does the book name as molecules in the food we eat? Select every correct answer.
opts: Proteins, in eggs, nuts, beans and meat
Carbohydrates, in bread, potatoes and pasta
Fats, such as plant oils and animal fats
Neon, in the air we breathe in
Gold, in a nugget from a stream
items.why: Proteins are large molecules. Bread, potatoes and pasta are made of complex molecules called carbohydrates, and another kind of complex molecule is fat. Neon and gold are elements, and neither is a food.

items.q: Why does the book say scientists use models?
opts: Because some things are too big or too small to see
Because a model is faster to build than a real thing
Because rules require a model before an experiment
Because models are more accurate than measuring
items.why: When something in science is too big or too small to see, scientists use models. A visual model is another form of language shared by chemists — models help make things easier to understand.

items.q: Match each model or sight to what it shows.

cells: Two oxygen atoms bonded to one carbon atom
Two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom
A glowing sign whose gas is one kind of atom

items.why: A model of carbon dioxide shows two atoms of oxygen and one atom of carbon bonded together. Water is two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom. And matter made of a single type of atom, like the neon in a sign, is an element.

chemistry.title: The Language of Chemistry
vocab: the science of what matter is made of and how matter changes
a small particle of chemical matter
text: Chemistry is the science of what matter is made of and how matter changes. But no one person thought up the idea of chemistry or of matter. People who were interested in the subject shared their ideas with one another.

By 500 BCE ancient Greeks were sharing their ideas about matter. One man, Democritus, talked to his teacher, Leucippus. They agreed that all matter was made of particles too small to be seen. They could not see the particles. They could only talk about this idea.
Democritus and Leucippus needed a name for these particles. The Greek prefix a- means “not,” and temnein means “to cut.” If you put the words together, you get atomos. Atomos means “not to cut.”

dalton.title: John Dalton Explained the Atomic Theory
text: The language of chemistry began and grew in ancient Greece. The ancient Greeks had a problem, though. They did not use a scientific process for examining ideas for supporting evidence. They did not determine whether their ideas were true or false.
Democritus is known as the “Father of the Atom.” However, it took about two thousand years before there was evidence to support the atomic theory of matter.

John Dalton was an English schoolteacher who studied the atom in 1808. He described matter as being made up of small particles called atoms. Unlike the ancient Greeks, he studied evidence from chemical reactions.

Dalton developed what we now call the atomic theory. It was built upon the ideas of Democritus: that atoms are tiny particles that cannot be further cut. But Dalton added to this idea. Dalton said that some atoms are alike and some are different. When atoms join, they make up different types of matter.

element.title: An Element Is Matter Made of a Single Type of Atom
vocab: a substance made of a single type of atom
text: Today, scientists have found 118 different kinds of atoms. Everything in the universe is made of the same 118 atoms. Only about 94 of the atoms are found naturally on Earth. Some atoms are made by people in special laboratories.

Matter is sometimes made of a single type of atom. When all the atoms in matter are the same, the matter is called an element. If we could see all the atoms in a single element, they would all be the same.
The glow of a neon sign is a beautiful sight. Likewise, all of the atoms that make up a gold nugget are atoms of the element gold.

bond.title: Atoms Bond Together to Form Molecules
vocab: a connection that holds atoms together
a substance made of one or more kinds of atoms joined together by chemical bonds
text: The element that occurs the most in the universe is hydrogen. Hydrogen gas is found in the stars and the sun. Most of the planet Jupiter is made of hydrogen gas. Hydrogen gas is two hydrogen atoms joined together.

When atoms like hydrogen atoms join, they form a bond. A chemical bond is a connection that holds atoms together. In oxygen gas, two oxygen atoms are connected by a chemical bond. When one or more kinds of atoms form chemical bonds with other atoms, they form molecules.

In hydrogen gas and oxygen gas, atoms of the same kind form chemical bonds. Atoms of different elements can bond together too. Much of the hydrogen on Earth is found in a bond with another element. Two hydrogen atoms often join with one oxygen atom. When this happens, you get a molecule of a substance you use every day. Water!

living.title: Molecules Are Important for Living Things
text: While elements represent the different basic types of matter, molecules make up almost all the matter we see every day. The matter that makes up a sidewalk, a building, or a bedspread is all composed of molecules.

Importantly, the food we eat is composed of molecules. Eggs, nuts, beans, and meat have lots of protein in them. Proteins are large molecules. Bread, potatoes, and pasta are made of complex molecules called carbohydrates. Another kind of complex molecules are fats, such as plant oils and animal fats.

Chemical changes occur in our bodies. The molecules of the food we eat are broken apart and then combine to form new chemicals. These chemical changes give us energy and the materials our bodies need to stay alive.

models.title: Models Help Us Understand Molecules
text: When something in science is too big or too small to see, scientists use models. In a way, a visual model is another form of language shared by chemists. Models help make things easier to understand. Scientists use models of molecules to show how the atoms are joined together.

Carbon dioxide is a molecule. Many of them form carbon dioxide gas. It has no color and no odor. When you breathe out, you breathe out carbon dioxide gas. Plants use it to make food. Carbon dioxide is one of the most common molecules in the world. It is found in the air and in the water.
A model of carbon dioxide helps us to understand that it is made of two atoms of oxygen and one atom of carbon that are bonded together.
